text:
sam: Heads-up: found a race in python async SDK when running multiple AsyncClient instances with different api_key values. Occasionally requests are sent with the wrong Authorization header and return 401s.

lisa: Can you reproduce locally?

sam: Yep, small script creating two AsyncClient(api_key=...) and asyncio.gather on generate. Intermittent.

maria: Likely shared aiohttp session headers being mutated per-request.

lisa: Short-term workaround: build per-request headers and call the low-level send with explicit headers (not great).

sam: Pushed a failing test to the repo. CI shows the 401 flake.

maria: Proposal: stop mutating session.headers, add `api_key` kwarg to public async methods, and an `AsyncClient.with_api_key()` async context manager that sets task-scoped creds. Also update .pyi stubs and add a concurrency smoke test.

ci-bot: Created issue github.com/redwood/inference/issues/2178 "async sdk auth header race; per-request override + context manager"

lisa: Agreed. I'll pick up the patch to avoid mutating session state and add the context manager API.

sam: Please add a small onboarding note in the Python quickstart about key rotation patterns.
